content.comment_body: Is it possible to connect a 4-20 mA signal directly to the analog input of [product_name]? Or does the signal need to be converted to 0-10 Volt first?

The analog input of a [product_name] basic module only supports 0-10V signals. If you want to use a current signal such as 0/4-20mA, you need to convert it to a voltage signal. One simple way is to use a 500 ohm resistor; as current passes through the resistor, it creates a voltage drop (0/2-10V) that the analog input can read. Note: not all basic modules have analog inputs, only those operated with DC supply voltage.
Thanks! I noticed that 4-20 mA sensor type appears in the analog input options of [product_name] software. I now realize this is just a label and not an actual feature of the hardware.

The 4-20 mA sensor type is included in the software because analog expansion modules like [product_name] type AM2 are available. AM2 modules provide two analog inputs that accept both 0-10V and 0/4-20mA signals. For PT100 sensors, there is also an analog extension module called AM2 RTD.
Thank you for clarifying! I understand now.
Should the 500 ohm resistor be placed in series or parallel with the sensor?

The resistor is connected in parallel with the analog input. The sensor and [product_name] must share the same power source. Attached is an example diagram showing how to connect a two-wire sensor to the analog input at connector I7.

analysis.insight_summary: Participants are asking for advice on how to connect 0/4-20 mA current signals to the analog inputs of [product_name] modules. Confusion has arisen because the configuration software presents current input options, although the hardware typically only accepts voltage inputs. Users also require detailed wiring instructions for adapting current signals to be compatible with these modules.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect [product_name] analog inputs or related modules to natively accept 4-20 mA signals as suggested by the software interface, and are seeking clear step-by-step guidance on how to wire these sensors properly.
